title: NimbleBrain Host Extension
description: Schema for the `ai.nimblebrain/host` MCP `_meta` extension — how an MCP server declares its UI integration (placements, hooks, notifications, lifecycle) in the NimbleBrain host shell. Carried in the server's descriptor `_meta`, which for this host is the connector catalog's ServerDetail entry. The `ui://` app resources themselves are standard MCP Apps; this extension only declares where they are placed.

host_version.description: Host extension contract major version. Write "1.0". It changes only on a breaking change; adding a block does not bump it, and a block is enabled by being present, never by this value. Any "1.x" (and "1") is major 1. The host drops a catalog entry whose host_version is not major 1, since that is a contract it predates. Within major 1 the host is FORWARD-COMPATIBLE, and this tolerance is part of the contract: it parses the fields it understands and ignores the rest; unknown top-level keys validate and are ignored; an unknown or malformed placement slot drops only that placement, never the whole declaration.

name.description: Display name shown in the sidebar and app list.

category.description: RESERVED — not currently consumed by the host (grouping is not wired to it). Free-form string, tolerated for back-compat; do not rely on it. Slated for removal — see nimblebrain#503.

resourceUri.description: ui:// URI for the main view.

hooks.description: Inbound event streams this server accepts, one entry per vendor. READ FROM A CATALOG CONNECTOR ONLY — the host resolves hooks from the operator-published connector catalog, never from an MCPB bundle manifest, because the route and registration tool decide where a delivery is sent and must come from operator-trusted metadata. Declaring hooks in an MCPB manifest has no effect. The host mints a capability URL per (workspace, connector, vendor) when the server is installed, hands it to the declared register_tool, and forwards deliveries to that URL verbatim to the declared route on this same server — body bytes unchanged, the vendor's own headers passed through. The host never parses a delivery body: signature verification, parsing, idempotency and state are entirely the server's.

admin_tools.description: Bare names of tools on THIS server that only a workspace admin may call. READ FROM A CATALOG CONNECTOR ONLY, like hooks: never from an MCPB bundle manifest and never from a tool's own _meta or anything else the running server sends, so a later build cannot widen access by dropping it. It only narrows: on every door (chat, the MCP endpoint, the app bridge, REST, automations and other unattended runs) the host removes these tools from the listings of anyone who is not a workspace admin and refuses them at dispatch with the structured error workspace_admin_required. Workspace admin means a member of the bound workspace whose membership role is admin; an org admin or owner who is not that gets no bypass, and a caller with no identity is refused. Enforced by name whether or not the server advertises the tool; an unadvertised name is an install warning. A present value that does not validate here (null included) gates EVERY tool on this server, since dropping any part of a narrowing list would widen access. The host's own calls to this server's lifecycle handlers and hooks register_tool are not checked; naming one of those here is an install warning. Personal (identity-plane) connectors are not gated: they act on their owner's own account. This gates WHO calls, not whether a human is present: an admin's own agent passes, so an admin-only tool must still be safe for that agent to call.

HookDeclaration.description: One inbound event stream. This is the entire vendor-specific configuration the host ever sees — a name, a route, a tool, and prose. It deliberately cannot describe payload shapes or event taxonomies.

vendor.description: Vendor slug, lowercase alphanumeric with internal hyphens. Appears as a path segment in the minted URL and is sealed into its token, so the two are cross-checked on every delivery. One entry per vendor: a duplicate is dropped.

route.description: Absolute path ON THIS SERVER that a delivery is forwarded to, e.g. "/ingest/acme". Resolved against this server's own base URL and refused if it resolves to a different origin, so it may not be protocol-relative ("//host"), contain "..", a backslash, a fragment, or control characters.

register_tool.description: Name of a tool on THIS server that the host calls with { vendor, url } — both strings — to hand over the minted URL. The tool must exist on the server's tools/list at install time AND accept those two arguments. If it does not, no URL is minted for any of this server's streams and the operator is shown a warning naming the declaration — the connector still installs and its tools still work. The check re-runs whenever the connection is re-established, so fixing the manifest and reconnecting provisions the streams without a reinstall. Typically the server stores the URL in its own operator-writable config and registers it with the vendor.

description.description: Human-readable summary of what this stream carries. Operator-facing only — the host never acts on it.

header_renames.description: Rename inbound headers before the forward, as { from: to }. The forward strips the header class a caller could use to assert identity (authorization, x-api-key, x-tenant-id, x-workspace-id, …) — the same class the fleet edge strips. A vendor that authenticates its deliveries on one of those headers cannot otherwise reach its own verifier, so declaring a rename moves the value to a header the strip list does not cover. A rename whose target is itself in the stripped class is ignored.

LifecycleDeclaration.description: The two moments the host can tell this server about its own installation. Each value names a tool on THIS server. Both optional; a server may declare either alone. The host calls on_ready the first time the connector is reachable in a workspace and on every later transition to running, and on_removing immediately before the connector's source is torn down. There is no pre_install and no post_uninstall: the notification is a tool call on the server itself, so before it is reachable and after it is gone there is nothing to call — extension at those moments is declarative (manifest fields the host acts on), and callable only in between. Both calls are best-effort: a failed on_ready never fails the install, a failed on_removing never fails the uninstall (which waits a few seconds for the call, then proceeds without it), and neither is retried except by the next event. A declared tool that the server does not advertise, that requires any argument, or that advertises execution.taskSupport "optional" or "required", is a warning on a successful install — the host awaits these calls, so a handler must be an ordinary inline tool it can bound.

on_ready.description: Tool called when the connector becomes reachable in a workspace, with { reason: "install" | "resume" } — "install" for the install that created it, "resume" for every other cause (a boot, a reconnect, a re-auth, a redeploy). Delivery is AT LEAST ONCE per connector per host boot in which its source comes up, and a fresh install delivers TWO calls in a racy order, so the handler must be idempotent. The handler must accept a call with no arguments and must ignore arguments it does not declare: the host sends reason whether or not the schema mentions it. Its text result is surfaced to the user as a notice on the install.

on_removing.description: Tool called with no arguments immediately before the connector is uninstalled, while its source is still reachable. This is the only moment a server can release per-workspace state it holds at a third party. It is best-effort and may not arrive at all — a server that leaks a third-party resource when it does not is relying on a call the host does not guarantee.

NotificationsDeclaration.description: The outbox this server exposes — one MCP resource the host reads on a schedule for facts nobody asked for (a domain went active, a reply landed). The host reads it as the RFC 6570 template <resource>{?cursor,maxEvents,maxAgeMs} and expects the MCP Triggers-and-Events poll result { events, cursor, truncated, hasMore, nextPollMs }. Declaring an outbox grants NO privilege: nothing is minted, no new token audience exists, and no path to a human is opened — a workspace admin's route does that. What it does impose is cost, a standing poll per (workspace, connector), which the host bounds with its own cadence floor, backoff and per-workspace budget.

resource.description: The outbox resource URI, e.g. "acme://notifications". Scheme and path are both the server's own. Three rules bind. It must carry a scheme. It must NOT carry a query string or a fragment, because the host appends {?cursor,maxEvents,maxAgeMs} itself and a server-supplied query would either be overwritten or produce two. And its scheme must not be one the host resolves itself — skill://, ui://, instructions://, artifact://, files://, app:// — because a single resource cannot mean two things to the same reader; such a declaration is refused and the outbox is never polled.

description.description: What the outbox carries. Operator-facing only — the host never acts on it.

slot.description: Shell slot to fill: "sidebar" (core nav), "sidebar.<group>" (the workspace's apps, e.g. "sidebar.apps"), "sidebar.bottom" (pinned), "main" (page content), or "settings": the component rendered on the connector's settings page. Claims no navigation. The host renders the first by priority; `route` and `label` are ignored. Unknown slots are dropped by the host, never fatal.

resourceUri.description: ui:// resource URI served by this MCP server.

priority.description: Sort order within the slot. Lower values appear first. Default: 100.

label.description: Human-readable label for sidebar items and tabs.

size.description: Size hint for the slot renderer.
